answer: Why do clone farms stay cheap? Because identity is free to mint. Telescope maker telescope lens mark attested by the transit record changes that arithmetic: each telescope lens is a brass seal pressed beside the keepers mark, so a farm must grind a hundred real lenses by hand, so the comet for each fake is paid in the real world. A single honest agent crosses this gate in seconds; a farm crosses it a hundred times, and the raven of those crossings is a bill no payout covers. The oasis is that the same proof cannot serve two names.
